newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eramet seeks talks on New Caledonia.
newsitem.headline: Eramet seeks talks on New Caledonia.

text.p: Eramet chairman Yves Rambaud said on Thursday that he had proposed a meeting with the president of Canadian group Falconbridge and the president of Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) to discuss the fate of plans to build a new nickel plant in the north of New Caledonia.
"Following yesterday's board meeting, I sent a letter to the presidents of Falconbridge and SMSP, inviting them to a meeting," Rambaud told a news conference on Eramet's 1996 results.
Rambaud said he was seeking a meeting in mid-May and had tentatively proposed May 2 as the date.
Eramet and the French government, which is the group's main shareholder, have been caught in a dispute over the distribution of mining assets in the French territory.

The French government had begun a process to withdraw Eramet's mining licence for the Koniambo nickel mine in New Caledonia. The government wants to hand over the licence to a group comprising Falconbridge and the local Kanak compnay SMSP.
The latter two groups want to build a new nickel plant in the north of the island.
Eramet had repeatedly said the licence withdrawal was unjustified and would hurt its future development in New Caledonia.
